page.layout: One column of running text, printed page 288. Nothing in the margins. Catchword "tum" at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.p: ritas ipsa, & mixta cum rabie inconsideran-tia suggerebant, sed [illegible, ~9 letters] omnia effudisti, & canis properans cœcos genui-sti catulos. Sicque, vt video, maiorem dif-fertationis tuæ partem ad astruendum inter Græcos, & Latinos diffidium, hinc inde ex varijs auctoribus Latinis, Græcis, Orienta-libus, etiam Pontificijs, recentioribus quo-que Romanensibus, Allatio [illegible, ~8 letters], & alijs vndique cogis, & auxilia comparas, in quibus magnum quid tibi polliceris, cum posthinc ad obiecta tibi ab Allatio deuolas, vel non respondens, vel in alia atque alia intempestiue subsultans, & nihil ad rem afferens, ita vt vbi ratio, & verba opus sunt, mutus atque elinguis deprehendaris. Quamuis modice me similia tangant, attamen vt tua nunc recens dicta priori congressu omnes noscant, habeto tibi quas infra scripsi notulas, cogor siquidem respondere stulto iuxta stultitiam suam, sed non stulte.

Leo Allatius Roma a Pontifice Romano huc ablegatus eam Bibliothecam diripuit. Bibliothecam Palatinam, & multitudine manuscriptorum Codicum tum Græcorum, tum Latinorum, aliarumque etiam linguarum, & singularium Codicum copia fuisse celeberrimam, non nego. Eam tamen a milite Bauaro spolium factam, Maximilianus tum

page.notes: Greek words in the first paragraph (after "sed" and the one after "Allatio") are not legible enough to copy letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The original has a Greek word after "sed" beginning with alpha and a Greek word after "Allatio" that looks like a case-inflected form; neither can be read with confidence. The dash before "Leo Allatius" appears to be a printed paragraph mark and is not transcribed. The catchword "tum" is the first word of the next page.
